title: Master episode spec (episode.json)
description: One file per episode, long film or part, on any of the four channels. It says what the episode is before anything is built: the question, the format, the voice, the look, the beats and where its other files live. The channel's own compile step still writes film.json (the clock the renderer reads); this file is the plan that compile step follows. Written by films/channels/studio/tools/new_episode.py, checked by films/channels/studio/tools/validate.py. How to use it: films/channels/studio/NEW-EPISODE.md. Keys that start with 'x-' are free for a channel's own notes.

id.description: <prefix>-s<season>e<nn>, for example ss-s3e01. The prefix is the channel identity's prefix (ss, rr, pl, oo). A season's long film takes number 00, for example pl-s3e00.

channel.description: Channel slug. An identity file films/channels/studio/identities/<slug>.json must exist. Adding a fifth channel means adding its identity file and its slug here.

number.description: Order inside the season, from 1. For a part it is the part number. 0 is the season's long film.

folder.description: Folder name on the channel's branch, under the identity's filmsPath. Episodes and parts: epNN, two digits (Prism imports only those). A long film: its name under compilations/, lower case with hyphens. No spaces: Prism's media push skips names with spaces.

title.description: Working title until status.title is 'chosen'. The final title is the winner in packaging.json (films/channels/PACKAGING.md asks for 35 to 55 characters). A part's title must equal its line in the long film's chapters.txt exactly, or Prism will not link them.

topic.description: The subject, in plain words, as the owner gave it.

question.description: The one question the episode answers. One story per episode.

hook.description: The first line and the first picture. For a short, a question spoken by 2.0 s (kits/cinema/script/WRITING.md).

payoff.description: What the viewer knows or feels at the end that they did not at the start. The like/follow moment comes after it.

beats.description: The story in order. Windows are a plan until the voice is measured; they must run from 0 to the planned length with no gap or overlap.

thread.description: Optional. One sentence: the single thread from hook to payoff.

script.description: The script in the kit's format (kits/cinema/script/README.md). Usually script.md.

packaging.description: out/packaging.json for an episode or part; packaging.json for a long film (films/channels/PACKAGING.md).

files.description: Paths relative to the episode folder.

assumptions.description: Everything that was defaulted or guessed rather than decided, one sentence each. An empty list means every value here was decided by a person or read from a file.

aiVoice.description: True when any narration in the delivered file is synthetic, including a stand-in voice or a clone of the owner's own voice.

aiVisuals.description: True when any AI-made image appears in the picture, whole or in part (films/channels/studio/SHOTS.md, 'Owner-made AI art'). The compile step copies it to film.json disclosures.aiVisuals, which Prism reads.

labels.description: The exact label lines the episode carries on screen or in its description.

disclosures.description: What the episode must tell viewers. Optional in the schema; validate.py warns when it is missing.

film.description: The long film's id or folder name.

partOf.description: For a part: which long film it is cut from (films/channels/SEASON-FORMAT.md).

created.description: Date the spec was first written, YYYY-MM-DD.

generatedBy.description: The tool and inputs that wrote the first version.

kind.description: short: a 9:16 episode of about 61 to 75 s (Seasons 1 and 2). premium: a Skin Sense Season 3 lesson, 9:16, 70 to 90 s. part: one of the 8 chapters of a long film, 9:16, 1:01 to 1:15. long: a 16:9 film or joined long video, 8:30 to 9:30.

aspect.description: Each aspect is its own composition, never a crop of the other.

size.description: [width, height] in pixels of the delivered master, the file Prism imports.

nativeSize.description: [width, height] the picture is really rendered at. Today the renderer's final tier draws 1080x1920 or 1920x1080 only (kits/cinema/film/render.mjs). When nativeSize is smaller than size, the master is an upscale and must be labelled as one.

durationS.description: [shortest, longest] allowed length in seconds for this format on this channel, copied from the channel identity. validate.py fails a window wider than the identity's.

targetS.description: The length the plan aims for, in seconds.

durationForced.description: True when the target was accepted outside durationS on purpose (new_episode.py --force). It covers planning only: validate.py warns instead of failing until stage 'editing', and fails from then on. A long video under 510 s and a premium lesson under 60 s fail even when forced.

deliveries.description: Every file the episode ships, with whether its pixels are native or an upscale.

kind.description: tts: a synthetic voice. owner: the channel owner. guest: another real person, with their written OK.

id.description: The voice's id: a synthetic voice name, or the folder the recordings live in.

wpm.description: The voice's reading pace in words a minute, as the channel identity and films/channels/voice-scripts/make_recording_script.py use it. Word budget = runtime in minutes x wpm x talkShare.

talkShare.description: The share of the runtime the voice is speaking. 1 for shorts and parts (kits/cinema/script/lint.py estimates length the same way); lower for ASMR lessons and long films, which leave picture-only time.

name.description: The speaker's name, when they are credited.

synthetic.description: True when the audio is generated, including a clone of the owner's own voice. Then disclosures.aiVoice must be true. Never true for a guest: a guest's voice is never synthesised.

standIn.description: The synthetic voice used for drafts until the recording arrives. Always labelled as AI.

consent.description: For a guest or a cloned voice: where the written OK is recorded, or a TODO for the owner. An owner's cloned voice cannot reach export while this holds a TODO.

season.description: Which look from the channel identity: a seasonLooks key such as s3, or base for the channel's standing identity.

palette.description: Token name to #RRGGBB. Only this channel's colours.

status.description: The season look's own status in the identity file, for example 'approved' or 'pending look gate'.

loudnessLufs.description: Integrated loudness target on the delivered AAC. kits/cinema/film/qa.py passes -15 to -13.

sound.description: The channel's sound, with any change for this episode.

id.description: The beat's heading in script.md. Letters, digits and underscores only, no hyphen: Prism's importer reads the heading as \w+ (prism-studio/scripts/import-episodes.ts) and drops a beat it cannot read.

purpose.description: The beat's job in the story.

words.description: Word budget for the beat at the voice's pace.

lines.description: Narration line ids spoken in this beat.

line.description: The like/follow line as spoken on the master (the 'follow' wording). From films/channels/CTA.md.

at.description: Where it goes, in words. Shorts: right after the payoff, about 70 to 85% through, never in the first 20 s.

section.description: The heading in films/channels/CTA.md the line came from.

variants.description: The same line for TikTok and Instagram (follow) and for the YouTube file (subscribe).

moments.description: Long videos have two moments. List both here; 'line' repeats the first.

stage.description: The pipeline stage the episode is in: concept, research, narrative, script, storyboard, visual production, motion, narration and sound, editing, QA, export, archiving.

lookGate.description: The owner's approval of this episode's stills (and, for Skin Sense Season 3, a 10 s clip) before the full render. Only the owner sets 'approved'.

sources.description: ok only when a person has opened every source in claims.json. A search excerpt is not enough.

title.description: chosen when the owner has picked the packaging winner.

recording.description: For an owner or guest voice: whether the real recording has arrived. A guest-voiced episode needs 'received' from stage 'editing' on.
